problem: Prior language-guided navigation work combines VLMs with fine-tuning, mapping modules or spatial-reasoning add-ons, so it is unclear how much frozen pretrained VLM embeddings alone can support navigation.
motivation: System designers face a tradeoff between complexity and performance, especially under limited compute. The paper isolates the contribution of frozen VLM embeddings by distilling a privileged expert into a reactive policy that sees only a single-frame embedding.
key_idea: Train a small feedforward behavior-cloning policy on the L2-normalized sum of frozen SigLIP image and text embeddings, with demonstrations from a privileged PPO expert.
insight: Frozen embeddings support basic language-to-visual grounding (74% SR) but yield trajectories 3.2x longer than the expert, since a reactive single-frame policy has no memory or planning. The multi-VLM comparison shows SigLIP (74%) > CLIP (62%) > ViLT-VQA (40%), matching the spatial sensitivity test ranking and embedding size (1152 vs 512 vs 768 dims) only loosely. BC loss is inversely related to navigation success, so it is not predictive. Prompts with relative spatial cues were crucial, since color-only prompts performed much worse.
method: Privileged expert: a PPO policy with full state and target identity/position gives 100% SR and generates ~500 demonstrations (100 per target color).
Language instructions: templated text giving target color and relative direction (left/right/straight ahead) computed from the robot heading.
Frozen SigLIP encoding: image and text embeddings (1152-d) are each L2-normalized, summed and re-normalized into a joint vector o.
BC policy: a feedforward MLP maps o to 2-D wheel velocities, trained with MSE and Adam (lr 1e-3, decayed).
VLM selection: a spatial sensitivity test (3x3 grid, cosine distance for same vs different cell) compares ViLT, CLIP and SigLIP; separate policies are then trained for each.

setting.backbone: SigLIP So400M-Patch14-384 (frozen) + feedforward MLP BC policy (trained from scratch); ViLT-VQA and CLIP ViT-B/32 as variants
setting.training_data: ~500 expert trajectories (tens of thousands of state-action pairs) from a PPO privileged expert in Isaac Sim
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged state only for the expert that generates training demonstrations)

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 test episodes with random start poses in a 3m x 3m arena with 5 colored spheres
numbers.extra: Expert pi_beta with privileged state: SR 100, avg timesteps 113.97; max 1000 timesteps, success radius 0.1 m
numbers.evidence: Table 2: Performance comparison between policies; learned policy 74.0 SR, 369.4 avg timesteps

numbers_note: Custom toy simulation benchmark, not a standard one. Model comparison numbers are given in text and a figure caption; the table shows only the SigLIP vs expert comparison.
results: The SigLIP-BC policy reaches 74.0% SR vs 100% for the privileged expert, but needs 369.4 vs 113.97 average timesteps (3.2x). It beats CLIP (62%) and ViLT (40%) trained the same way.
limitations: Very simple environment: flat 3m arena, 5 colored spheres, no obstacles, single simulator, no real robot.
Reactive single-frame policy lacks memory and planning, causing circling, target confusion, timeouts and long paths; success depends on hand-designed spatial-cue prompts.
No comparison against fine-tuned or mapping-based navigation baselines; only 100 evaluation episodes.
